prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room), Main Transformer (monitored; abnormal trends escalated; protection settings separately approved), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; Dispatcher sets permitted export; relay applies ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized switching plan). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Turbine Lockout stays until responsible authority confirms safe. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image; deferred if uncertain visibility). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Substation Operator: switching, clearances after authorization. Control Engineer: stepwise actions, hold points, software changes, remote shutdown, guidance when recovery affects turbine/restart. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarm priority safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; flags reschedulable tasks), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Operations Radio Console, Warehouse System, Spares Hub. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy (discrepancies→review age/location). Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note (estimate+confidence)→Duty Planner. Low confidence is a constraint; point estimate alone can't authorize; visual tasks assessed conservatively; go/no-go weighs method, competence, vessel, confidence. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation, assigns vessels, approach plan, reviews uncertainty impact, pauses recovery on deterioration and agrees holding position with Vessel Master. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console; may decline. Rescue Coordinator: recovery plan, Recovery Basket Load Sheet (from Service Operations Vessel). Duty Planner:

New part:
S677: The Vessel Master retains authority to proceed, slow, alter course, or hold position based on actual conditions and vessel limits.
S678: A Crew Transfer Vessel may be directed to remain clear of a transfer location until the crew and vessel can maintain adequate visual awareness.
S679: A Daughter Craft operation requires particular caution where reduced visibility could compromise separation from other vessels or structures.
S680: A Service Operations Vessel may maintain a safe stand-off while the visibility assessment is clarified.
S681: Planned vessel movements account for reduced speed, increased separation, and the possibility of returning to a safe holding area.
S682: When uncertainty increases during transit, the Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master reassess the route and the suitability of continuing toward the work site.
S683: The Shore Control Room maintains awareness of the decision and the operational restrictions associated with the assessment.
S684: A no-go decision is appropriate when uncertainty prevents the team from demonstrating that the transfer or task can be completed within safe limits.
S685: Conditions are reassessed before work resumes, and authorization is based on current evidence rather than the earlier estimate.
S686: The inventory record covers serviceable parts, consumables, repairable units, and their locations across shore and offshore stores.
S687: Warehouse System maintains the authoritative item catalogue, stock balances, and storage locations.
S688: Stock visibility includes quantities on hand, items reserved for approved work, and quantities already committed to transfer.
S689: Spares Hub provides a separate view of stock held for regional replenishment and emergency support.
S690: The Storekeeper reconciles physical counts with recorded balances and records adjustments with a reason and timestamp.
S691: Each stocked item is identified by a controlled part number, description, unit of measure, and approved substitute status.
S692: Serial-controlled parts retain traceability from receipt through installation, repair, return, or disposal.
S693: Reservations prevent the same available quantity from being assigned to multiple work packages.
S694: Maintenance Planning Engine uses planned work demand and part criticality to support replenishment forecasts.
S695: The Duty Planner reviews forecast demand against current stock before confirming work readiness.
S696: Priority is highest for safety-critical parts and parts required to restore a turbine or electrical system to service.
S697: Parts supporting scheduled maintenance receive priority when their delivery date is necessary to protect an approved work window.
S698: Routine consumables are replenished according to agreed minimum and maximum stock levels.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
